notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Private cars carry yellow plates, almost unique in South America.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Taxis are a pastel yellow with white plates, often printed on the side and roof, sometimes with the city name.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 can show a short thick antenna on a black, white or grey car; only here is it on a black car.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 4 is commonly a white or silver car.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: White metal signposts form a distinct cross on the back of signs.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Kilometre markers are either a tall green post with "Pr" at the top or a stone marker with black lettering; both are unique.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles often have black-and-yellow or black-and-orange stripes.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Mostly concrete poles with varied tops; octagonal ones are found, as in Mexico and Ecuador, and dark poles are common.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Wooden fences are very common; painted posts that are sharp on top are almost exclusive here.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Sidewalks are often decorated with reddish tiles.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: White sandy soil and arid land in the north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Open tropical grasslands and savanna with scattered trees east of the Andes, with seasonal flooding.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Extremely dry land with low vegetation and occasional cacti in La Guajira.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole markings with short black strips top and bottom and a long yellow section are common in Antioquia.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Sugar cane grows along the Cauca river in Valle del Cauca and nearby.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The narrow land bridge near Barranquilla has dashed yellow lines and shallow water on both sides.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Small concrete poles bearing street names mark intersections in Barranquilla.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A camera glitch makes part of the image look oversaturated in the south.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Caribbean islands San Andrés and Providencia have coverage with unique cars; Providencia has green street lights.
